### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d9b9b47f4798aa2d819f64be13459afcef25d38` — the merge of head `c4bbb0adeae3326cd6975f0a2c891df974607c45` into base `d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d9b9b47f4798aa2d819f64be13459afcef25d38 && git checkout 7d9b9b47f4798aa2d819f64be13459afcef25d38
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d c4bbb0adeae3326cd6975f0a2c891df974607c45 && git checkout -B drift-repro d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d && git merge --no-ff c4bbb0adeae3326cd6975f0a2c891df974607c45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

- **Gates:** check-runs on this head: 57 success, 8 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. `Build Core`'s `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` step concluded success, which closes the one local NOT MEASURED.
- **Follow-up filed by the seat:** the `FlowSchema` `@example` in `flow.zod.ts` (around L1070) has the same unguarded edges. It is not refused today only because its start node has no `objectName`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c4bbb0adeae3326cd6975f0a2c891df974607c45`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts + content/docs/references/data/validation.mdx (generated from it), packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts (`isNullableField` is in validate-expressions.ts ≈L483, `truthGuards` ≈L512, `provenNonNullKeys` ≈L605, `findUnguardedNullableOperands` ≈L639), packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (`rulePredicates` ≈L659, `buildNullableFieldIndex` ≈L2307, `checkNullGuards` ≈L2486, the flow null-guard block ≈L2959-L2977, the validation-rule walk ≈L3418-L3470), packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts (`gen:docs` / `check:docs`), skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md (≈L112-L122, ≈L399-L407), .changeset/31334-validation-amount-null-guard-example.md, and the seven docs pages (content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx, flows.mdx, hook-bodies.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx, validation.mdx, content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx), widened in because the card's table names every one of them and the seat asked for each site to be judged. Cited code read on `origin/main` `d0512c2fb`; the merge base is `dc7f5c4b4`, and none of the five commits between them touches a file in the diff or a cited file. Face: schema (`record-recognisers --paths` over the nine files returns the one hit, `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts`). No governed-register path is in the diff.

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #31334 (body, triage audit 6716403823, the seat's claim 6716759332, the os-dev report 6717074863), the PR body and file list (9 files, +31 / −16), the net diff against the merge base, PR #31322 and its record 6715980957 for context, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run: this container has no installed dependencies (empty `node_modules`, a 23 MB pnpm store), so the dev's probe could not be re-executed without an install and a three-package build; each site was instead traced through the rule's own code, named below, and the dev's probe table on the PR body was checked against the trace.

- **No accept set moves.** RIGHT. `validation.zod.ts` changes three strings: the `.describe()` of `ScriptValidationSchema.condition` (L180) and two TSDoc examples (`cross_field` ≈L257, `conditional` `then` ≈L532). The schema stays `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema`, inside the same `strictObject`; no refine, default, alias, export or type changes. The reference page's four changed rows (L170, L291, L505, L571) are the one describe string, verbatim, in the four nested-shape tables that render `ScriptValidation`.
- **Published description text changes, as a patch.** RIGHT. The string ships in the built json-schema projection (gitignored, `gen:schema`), the `.d.ts` doc comments and the generated reference page. The committed `json-schema.manifest/data.json` does not carry it. A grep over the head for the describe sentence outside those carriers finds nothing, so no test pins the old text.
- **The L180 example passes the rule it cites.** RIGHT, traced. `rulePredicates` yields the `script` rule's `condition`; `checkNullGuards` runs `findUnguardedNullableOperands` with `fail-closed`. `record.amount != null && record.amount < 0`: the `&&` visit hands the right conjunct `truthGuards(left)`, and `!=` against the null literal yields `{record.amount}`; the `<` operand is that key, so `report` returns before any finding. Before, on an object whose `amount` is `{ type: 'currency' }` with no `required`, `defaultValue`, default option or autonumber (`isNullableField` → nullable), the bare `<` is one finding. Matches the dev's 1 → 0.
- **The two doc-comment examples pass.** RIGHT, traced. `cross_field`: `((discount != null && amount != null) && discount > (amount * 0.40))` — `truthGuards` of the left conjunct is the union `{record.discount, record.amount}`, which covers the `>` operand and the `*` operand; before, both operands are findings (the dev's 2 → 0). `conditional`: `rulePredicates` recurses into `then` at depth 1 and `checkNullGuards` runs on it; `((amount != null && amount > 100000) && approval == null)` guards the `>` inside its own conjunction, and `==` is never flagged (1 → 0).
- **The six guarded docs sites pass, and each guard sits where the rule reads it.** RIGHT, traced.
  - `approvals.mdx` L145: `triggerType: 'record-after-update'` resolves to `record_change`, so the start condition is the trigger gate, judged with no presumption; `record.amount != null && record.amount >= 50000 && record.stage == 'proposal'` parses left-associative and the `>=` is inside the conjunction its guard dominates; the `==` is inert. The flow's edges carry labels, not conditions, so there is nothing downstream to presume. Guard on the start, as the ruling asks (`validate-expressions.ts` ≈L2967-L2976 passes `provenNonNullKeys(start)` as `presumed` to every edge and `decision` slot).
  - `flows.mdx` L2473: a start-node `condition` row in the syntax table; the guard dominates the `>`.
  - `hook-bodies.mdx` L74: hook `condition`, covered row; `record.status == "open" && record.amount != null && record.amount > 1000` — the last conjunct's guard set is `truthGuards(status == "open" && amount != null) = {record.amount}`.
  - `formulas.mdx` L119 and L356: field `requiredWhen`, covered row (fail-open, so an unguarded predicate enforced nothing); guard dominates.
  - `formulas.mdx` L394 and `validation.mdx` L329: `script` rule conditions, same trace as L180. The two added sentences under L394 state the gate's rule correctly (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` or arithmetic on a nullable field needs a null test first) and name no tracker number.
- **common-patterns declares `amount` `required: true` instead of a guard.** RIGHT, and it is the honest fix (judged in ④).
- **The reference page was regenerated, not hand-edited.** RIGHT. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:docs` (`build-docs.ts --check`) runs in `Type Check · source gates` as the step "Check generated reference docs are in sync with the spec"; that step is `continue-on-error`, so the job's green is not enough on its own — the step's own conclusion on this head is `success`. Independently, the page's only change is the describe string, byte-identical in all four rows, with no other hunk.
- **Labels.** `protocol:data` is on the PR, applied by `Auto Label` from `.github/labeler.yml` (`packages/spec/src/data/**`); `documentation`, `size/s` and `tooling` likewise. Nothing is owed by hand.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/spec': patch` is right. Ruling A in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads the level off the `Metadata-protocol:` line alone: `none` requires every introduced entry to be `patch` and no `authorable-surface/` baseline to move; both hold (the `check:authorable-surface` step is green on the head). `Clause-②: no` is right: description and doc-comment text only, no accept set widens or narrows, so no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed (that gate asks for one only on a declared breaking change). Both lines are line-initial in the changeset and in the PR body, and the changeset text names all three string changes, including the two doc comments. The docs pages belong to no published package, so no second changeset is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

On the spec-lane question: the card's suggested shape says the spec example "rides with a spec-lane note"; the triage ruling (6716403823) says only that it "rides the same PR as a spec doc-example change". No rule in AGENTS.md or os-dev.md owes a note of that name, the PR body states the spec-file change and the regeneration in both languages, and the `protocol:data` label is already applied. Not owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation: the two `validation.zod.ts` doc-comment examples (≈L257, ≈L532) are outside the card's table.** Accepted, on the code. os-dev.md's in-place exemption has four conditions and two debts: ① same defect class — yes (the same rule refuses both, by trace); ② mechanical fix with a pinned shape — yes (the formula skill's `record.x != null && …`); ③ no other claim on the file — yes (among open PRs only #31358 touches `validation.zod.ts`; #31322 touches `hook.zod.ts`); ④ same gate family, no new verification surface — yes. The debts: the claim already names the file (the claim's "(example string)" reads as the file's example strings; both additions are example strings in that file, so no amendment is needed), and the PR body names the fix with before/after evidence. No escalation.
- **The ruling "guard the start condition, not each edge" is followed.** `approvals.mdx` guards the start; `common-patterns.mdx` leaves its edges as written and removes the nullability instead, which is the one case where a start guard would have been the wrong fix (④).
- **Out of scope held.** No `ui/` file in the diff (the `SchemaForm.erasedArmMark-9830.test.tsx` constant is untouched); no release notes or CHANGELOG; `validation.mdx` L51 untouched (its one hunk is L329, and `amount` at L31 is `required: true` on main).
- **Labels not sent by `pr_create`.** The order named none and the relay refuses an empty list; `Auto Label` supplied them. Not a contract matter.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, prerequisite not met).** It runs in `ci.yml`'s `build-core` job (`Build Core`) on every PR. `Build Core` is green on this head, and its step "Every published require entry point actually loads" (`pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) concluded `success`, so the one locally not-measured gate is measured green in CI. Check-runs as read by this review: 65 runs, 57 success, 8 skipped (opt-in and schedule-gated jobs), 0 failure, 0 running, including all eight `Test Core` shards, the four `Type Check` jobs, every `Lint` job, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Docs`, `Live E2E UI` and `Build & E2E UI`.
- **Report's "PR #31322 touches none of these files".** True: #31322's files are `hook.zod.ts`, `hook.mdx`, the automation skill reference and its changeset.
- **`main` moved five commits since the base** (`dc7f5c4b4` → `d0512c2fb`); none touches a file in the diff or a cited lint or spec file. GitHub had not finished recomputing mergeability at read time; nothing in the moved commits can conflict.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` 1: `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts` ≈L1070 `FlowSchema` `@example`** spells `record.amount < 500` / `>= 500` on edges `e2` / `e3`. Confirmed on `main`: its start node carries no `config.objectName`, so `nullGuardObject` is undefined and the gate does not run; an author who binds it to an object with a nullable `amount` is refused. Not a defect of this PR and not in the card's table; should-fix for the seat, outside this PR: file it as a sibling card (spec `@example` text, `protocol:automation`), the way #31206 produced this card.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` 2** is the deviation above. **`open_questions`**: none. **Security**: none.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. No should-fix inside the PR.

- **`packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts`: holds.** Against the rule it cites: all three examples pass `findUnguardedNullableOperands` on an object whose `amount` (and `discount`) is nullable, by the traces in ①, and the dev's probe table agrees at every count. Against the first consumer: an author or agent who copies the describe example, the `cross_field` example or the `conditional` example into a `script` / `cross_field` rule on a nullable field now gets metadata that `os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` and the runtime publish gate accept, where before the write path faulted (`null < 0` has no overload) and the rule refused every row with a null `amount`, which is not what "amount must be non-negative" means. The guarded reading is the honest semantics: a null `amount` is the `required` check's business, not the sign check's. I tried to break it: the added text carries no quote character, so the single-quoted TS describe string and the backticked `P\`…\`` inside it keep their shape; `&&` and `!=` survive MDX escaping (the same form already renders in `hook.mdx`, and `Build Docs` is green); the `cross_field` `fields: ['discount', 'amount']` still names exactly the two operands; the `conditional` `when` is an equality the gate never flags; no other comparison in the file is unguarded.
- **`content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`: holds, and `required: true` is the right fix.** The flow branches on `amount` at `e2` / `e3`; its start condition is a state transition on `status`. A guard on the start condition (the ruling's default) would make a submitted report with no amount launch no flow at all: never auto-approved, never routed, with the write landing — the silent skip the dev names. Guarding each edge is what the ruling forbids, and a null would then match neither branch and strand the run at `check_amount`. Declaring `amount` required moves the refusal to the write, where the author sees it: an expense report without an amount is not a report. With it, `isNullableField` is false, `amount` leaves the nullable index, and `e2` / `e3` pass as written; `title` was already required and `status` has a default, so the object's shape stays coherent. The example has no seed to break, the flow's nodes and edges are untouched, and the `check_amount` decision node carries no `config`, so no `decision` slot is judged. The one-line comment says why the field is required, which is the teaching the page owes.
- **The six guarded pages: hold.** Each guard is in the slot the rule reads (start condition, hook condition, `requiredWhen`, `script` condition), spelled `record.x != null && …` as the formula skill teaches, and the `formulas.mdx` sentence under L394 states the gate correctly without restating the rule's provenance.

Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5njkh3xbcDN6EtSfw7`

**VERDICT: PASS**
